A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAM 2 and SA-V research. Their text, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original image/video segmentation experiments, data-engine measurements, fairness evaluation, and data and architecture ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical studies and reports updated segmentation results for the model identified as SAM 2.1.

M1.justification: v2 explicitly introduces an additional fine-tuning stage using 16-frame sequences, difficult masklets, and a frozen image encoder, extending v1's 8-frame training procedure. The revised training recipe adds mosaic augmentation, and Appendix D.1 additionally documents a learned occlusion embedding in memory. These materially extend the model's training procedure while retaining its streaming architecture and losses.

E1.justification: The training sources and evaluation coverage remain the same, including the 17 zero-shot video datasets, 37 image datasets, DAVIS interactive benchmark, and demographic evaluation. Longer training sequences and revised masklet sampling change settings within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain SAM+XMem++, SAM+Cutie, SAM/HQ-SAM, MiVOS/CiVOS, and the existing VOS baselines. Table 17c's SwinB-DeAOT becomes SwinB-DeAOT-L with identical reported scores; this is a naming clarification, not an added comparator.

E3.justification: The reported full-training schedule changes from approximately 300k steps and 15k warmup steps in v1 Table 13 to 150k and 7.5k in v2 Table 12. v2 adds 10% mosaic augmentation and 50k iterations of 16-frame fine-tuning at half the learning rate, selecting the most-edited 50% of SA-V/Internal masklets. Evaluation metrics and prompting protocols remain stable.

E4.justification: The extensive data, capacity, positional-encoding, memory, and fairness analyses are retained despite relocation. However, v2 removes v1 Appendix E.2's diagnostic comparison with an earlier model trained on fewer part annotations, which reported 0.86 AUC-J&F and 0.89 J&F@60s to support the explanation of DAVIS behavior.

E5.justification: Neither version reports run counts, seeds, or significance tests, and no uncertainty-reporting procedure is added or revised. Benchmark tables retain point estimates, and the data-scaling figure retains its existing shaded-band presentation.

E6.justification: Results are extensively revised for the updated model and training recipe. Table 4's 17-dataset averages change from 73.2 to 75.3 for three clicks and 77.6 to 79.3 for mask prompts; Table 14 changes from 0.84/0.87 to 0.86/0.90 for AUC-J&F/J&F@60s. Changes include regressions: Hiera-B+ DAVIS 2017 validation falls from 90.9 to 90.2, and Figure 15's maximum image gain falls from 53.9 to 41.1. These are revised-model results, not isolated same-training improvements.

T1.justification: The task definitions and annotation-time formulas are retained. Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs, and v2's new training explanations do not introduce formal mathematical results.

C1.justification: The core contributions—promptable visual segmentation, streaming-memory SAM 2, and SA-V—and the headline interaction and speed claims remain. The abstract and introduction expand the release contribution from a model version and interactive demo to main checkpoints plus training and demo source code, identifying the updated model as SAM 2.1.

C2.justification: v2 explains how mosaic augmentation encourages motion/temporal cues and small-object learning, and identifies the mismatch between short training clips and long-video inference as motivation for additional fine-tuning. The existing limitations and fairness interpretation are retained. The DAVIS part-versus-whole explanation remains, but its earlier-model verification is removed.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands the documented reproducibility resources by announcing training and demo source code alongside main checkpoints. Appendix D specifies the mosaic construction, difficult-masklet selection, fine-tuning duration, learning-rate reduction, encoder freezing, and 80 GB GPU constraint. It also clarifies manual-only video annotations and details independent per-object inference. Resource availability is assessed from these PDF statements only.

R1.justification: v2 removes the TrackFormer citation and bibliography entry associated with object pointers. Section 2 condenses the survey and drops the explicit characterization of joint-transformer VOS approaches as having prohibitive inference cost. The overall positioning relative to SAM and prior video segmentation remains.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: v1 Section 8's ablations become v2 Appendix A, fairness evaluation moves to Appendix E.1.1, and dataset-diversity discussion moves into the appendix. The zero-shot experiment hierarchy is simplified, related-work prose is condensed, and model-training explanations are expanded.

P2.justification: Numerous displays move with the reorganized material, including the ablation tables, scaling plot, fairness table, and dataset-distribution figure. The training hyperparameter table changes from side-by-side panels to stacked full-width panels. Figure 15 is reordered and rescaled, and architecture/display sizing is revised; these changes go beyond numerical substitutions and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The expanded code-release statement and explicit augmentation/fine-tuning recipe improve reproducibility, while the broad empirical evaluation is retained and updated. The benefit is limited by removal of the DAVIS diagnostic and incomplete reconciliation of results with prose: v2 still claims a maximum image gain of 53.9 although Figure 15 shows 41.1. The net improvement is modest rather than a substantial strengthening of the paper.
